portInfo.description: Lyttelton Port Company welcomes cruise guests as the gateway to Canterbury. LPC states its cruise berth is New Zealand’s first purpose-built cruise ship facility: 148 metres long, able to cater to the world’s largest cruise vessels up to 362 m long carrying up to 6,000 passengers and 2,000 crew, with a shoreside shelter for coach transfers and an amenities building. There is no walk-off access from the cruise berth; on ship days dedicated shuttles run to Lyttelton (Norwich Quay stop) and Christchurch (Cashel Street). Meeting parties should arrange to meet in town or the city centre, not at the berth.

facts.established: Established as a port in the 19th century
facts.significance: Main port for Christchurch and Canterbury region

politics.visaRequirements: Visa or NZeTA required for most visitors. NZeTA available online for many nationalities.
politics.entryRequirements: Valid passport required. NZeTA or visa required for most non-citizens.

gettingThere.distanceToCity: Use ship/LPC shuttles only from the berth.
gettingThere.publicTransport: Confirm local transport options with the ship on your call date.
gettingThere.distanceAnswer: Use ship/LPC shuttles only from the berth.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Christchurch city rebuild / gardens — ~180 min with shuttle.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Do not plan to walk off the berth — shuttle is mandatory.
